newsitem.title: FRANCE: RENAULT SHARES REBOUND AFTER VILVOORDE COMPROMISE.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT SHARES REBOUND AFTER VILVOORDE COMPROMISE.

text.p: Shares in Renault rebounded on Wednesday on the view that the French government did not appear to be pressuring the car-maker to scrap its controversial plan to close the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium.

In an apparent political compromise Renault said on Tuesday an independent study to explore alternatives to the proposed closure, which Renault insists is essential to streamline its European operations.
"The fact that the government hasn't tried to impose a continuation of the plant's activity will allow Renault to pursue a restructuring," one analyst said.
Its share price, which tumbled 4.63 percent on Tuesday on reports that the study would delay the closure, was up 2.66 percent at 131.20 francs at 1130 GMT.
"A fresh examination of the plant's situation by an independent expert represents a good solution," said another analyst.
Renault said the report was due before the end of June, angering union leaders who said that did not allow enough time for a serious exploration of alternatives.
If the study showed the plant should close, Renault said it would take measures to ease the social impact and help set up replacement industries.

A spokesman said the study would not add to the 2.42 billion franc cost of the closure provisioned in the 1996 results, but officials said it was premature to give any estimate of the cost to Renault of the establishment of another activity on the site.
French government officials also said it was premature to estimate the cost of such an activity and who would pay.

Brokers said the stock was also helped by Chairman Louis Schweitzer's remarks that there was a reasonable chance of breakeven for the car division for 1997 despite a deterioration in the French market.
Sales in the first five months of the year are down 23 percent from the year-earlier period.
Schweitzer told the annual general meeting on Tuesday that if the car division broke even, net and operating results would be positive this year.
